evidence: src/adapters/outbound/payment/CardPaymentAdapter.ts: class CardPaymentAdapter implements PaymentPort, an outbound port adapter, which fits the infrastructure role
authorise(): stores the reference and amount in a private Map, which simulates the provider's authorisation state
authorise(): `if (amountCents <= 0) return false;` is a gateway-style validity check, not a business policy decision
refund(): deletes the stored authorisation, which simulates a provider refund
parsedVerdict.reasoning: CardPaymentAdapter belongs to the adapters-outbound (infrastructure) layer. It implements the application-owned PaymentPort and works as an in-memory stand-in for an external card payment provider. Its methods are authorise, which records an authorisation in a Map, and refund, which removes it. Talking to an external system, or simulating one, is the job of an infrastructure adapter. The one conditional, `if (amountCents <= 0) return false;`, matches how a real payment gateway rejects an invalid amount. It does not decide anything about the business process, such as order rules, pricing or refund eligibility, so it does not move domain or application logic into infrastructure. There is no presentation or transport-to-client logic either.
